text:
toni: New hire hit a weird one — installed redwoodctl via company installer (Windows) and then opened WSL to try it. `redwoodctl` command not found in WSL PATH.

alex: If the Windows exe is installed under C:\Program Files, WSL won't expose it unless you call it with /mnt/c/... or add a wrapper. Symlinking the exe into /usr/local/bin will give Exec format errors.

toni: Yup I tried `ln -s` and got Exec format error. Ended up creating a small wrapper script in /usr/local/bin that calls the Windows exe: `#!/bin/bash
/mnt/c/Program Files/Redwood/redwoodctl.exe "$@"`. Works for now.

mira: Also watch credentials: browser auth from WSL opens Windows browser and the token ends up in %LOCALAPPDATA% so `redwoodctl whoami` in WSL still shows logged out. Device flow (`redwoodctl auth login --device`) writes to XDG path and avoids the mismatch.

toni: Can we add an installer option or a flag like `redwoodctl install --wsl-shim` that creates the wrapper automatically and optionally mirrors creds? That would reduce support tickets.

alex: Good idea. Mirror needs to be opt-in and atomic (write tmp then mv) to avoid races. Also add a `redwoodctl config sync` command to reconcile stores.

mira: Filed as DEVEX-4999 with steps and proposed UX.

dev-tools-bot: New ticket created: DEVEX-4999  Installer: detect WSL and offer `--wsl-shim` + optional credential mirror. Assigned to @mira.
